name: Korvel Yuzu-Black Sesame Bark
description: Snappable synth-white confection bark embedded with toasted black sesame clusters and a yuzu oil drizzle that pools in the cracks. Sold in irregular hand-broken pieces by weight.
flavor_profile: Bright yuzu citrus on first contact, rich roasted sesame in the body, creamy-sweet synth base that melts cleanly
slogan: Break a piece. Share or don't.
cultural_context: Korvel bark is sold by weight at market counters and through vending nodes that dispense pieces into paper cones. The irregularity of each piece is considered part of the appeal — it signals handcraft in a market flooded with machine-uniformity. Gifting a cone of Korvel bark is a casual but genuine gesture of affection in Tier 2 social contexts.
story_hooks: A Korvel market counter doubles as an informal message drop for a courier network that doesn't trust digital communication — specific sesame cluster patterns on the display slab signal different message types.
The yuzu oil in Korvel bark comes from a single licensed source, and when that source is bought out by a corponation and the formula changes, longtime customers immediately notice — and react badly.
A Tier 4 chef becomes obsessed with reverse-engineering Korvel's snap texture, convinced there's a proprietary synth-compound involved, and hires a food chemist to find out what they're missing.
